abstract: |
  NuSEDS (New Salmon Escapement Database System) escapement estimate type classification (Types 1--6) provides a standardized approach for describing the interpretability of salmon escapement estimates, supporting the application of these data in downstream processes in the Pacific Region (e.g., for stock assessment and Wild Salmon Policy status workflows). In practice, Type assignment has varied across programs as historical guidance does not explicitly address several common factors that can influence estimate interpretability including incomplete run-window coverage, outages and missed observation, breach and bypass events at counting sites, visibility constraints, and incomplete documentation. This technical report updates the Type 1--6 guidance by operationalizing the intent of Kim Hyatt's 1997 classification key as a property-first decision sequence. The updated key separates enumeration (field) methods from estimation (analysis) methods, defines method families, and records standardized qualifier codes that explain conservative downgrades related to timing, coverage/uptime, breach/bypass events, visibility, documentation, and quantified uncertainty (e.g., coefficient of variation [CV] and standard error [SE]). The report also identifies a minimal set of metadata elements needed for transparent Type assignment in NuSEDS, with an emphasis on Stream Escapement Narratives (SENs) and controlled vocabularies for downgrade criteria and uncertainty metrics. Adoption of this guidance is expected to improve cross-program consistency, increase transparency of classification decisions, and support more defensible downstream use of escapement estimates.

csas_kable <- function(x,
                       caption = NULL,
                       align = NULL,
                       escape = TRUE,
                       ...) {
  align_kable <- align
  if (!is.null(align) && length(align) > 1) {
    align_kable <- paste0(align, collapse = "")
  }

  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    csasdown::csas_table(
      x,
      format = "latex",
      caption = caption,
      align = align,
      escape = escape,
      ...
    )
  } else if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    knitr::kable(
      x,
      format = "html",
      caption = caption,
      align = align_kable,
      escape = escape
    ) |>
      kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
  } else {
    knitr::kable(
      x,
      caption = caption,
      align = align_kable,
      escape = escape
    )
  }
}

# Apply column width styling only for HTML/LaTeX outputs.
# For docx/officedown, keep tables plain to avoid HTML widget leakage.
csas_colspec <- function(tbl, column, width) {
  if (knitr::is_html_output() || knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    kableExtra::column_spec(tbl, column, width = width)
  } else {
    tbl
  }
}

widoco_term_link <- function(term) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(term) | term == "",
    "",
    sprintf(
      "[%s](%s)",
      term,
      paste0(
        "https://dfo-pacific-science.github.io/dfo-salmon-ontology/#",
        sub("^gcdfo:", "", term)
      )
    )
  )
}
